proposals.before: The Emperor secretly pleaded on their behalf, and they were banished—Youqiu to Fengzhou, Wei to Fengzhou, and Guangbin to Xiuzhou.
proposals.after: The Emperor secretly pleaded on their behalf, and they were banished—Youqiu to Fengzhou, Wei to Peak Prefecture (Fengzhou), and Guangbin to Xiuzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 暐於峰州 is Peak Prefecture, not the same Fengzhou (封州) as Youqiu's exile; the literal conflates both as Fengzhou.

proposals.before: He married into Ge Fushun's family; Shoude, Tang Diwen, son of Left Gate Guardian General Lu Longzi, the Left and Right Martial Guard generals Wang Jingyao and Gao Guangji, and dozens more relied on Maozhong in wrongdoing.
proposals.after: He married into Ge Fushun's family; Shoude, Left Gate Guardian General Lu Longzi Tang Diwen, the Left and Right Martial Guard generals Wang Jingyao and Gao Guangji, and dozens more relied on Maozhong in wrongdoing.
proposals.reason: Chinese 左監門將軍盧龍子唐地文 names one officer (appellation 盧龍子 + name 唐地文); the idiomatic English wrongly splits Lu Longzi as Tang Diwen's father.

decisions.reason: Chinese 流幽求於封州、暐於峰州 distinguishes Youqiu's 封州 from Wei's 峰州; the original literal wrongly renders both as Fengzhou, and Peak Prefecture (Fengzhou) correctly marks 峰州.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 流幽求於封州、暐於峰州、光賓於繡州

decisions.reason: Chinese 左監門將軍盧龍子唐地文 is one officer (title + appellation 盧龍子 + name 唐地文); the idiomatic wrongly invents a father–son split, and the proposed wording restores a single person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 左監門將軍盧龍子唐地文
